Let V (G) = {v1, . . . , vn} and let T1, . . . , Tn be subtrees of T in Λ satisfying vi ∼vj in G

for j = 2, . . . , n. We claim that v1 is simple in G. Suppose that vi, vj ∈NG(v1) and Ti > Tj.
It suffices to show that NG(vj) ⊆NG(vi). Since
dT(w1, r) ≥dT(wj, r)
and
V (T1) ∩V (Tj)̸ = ∅
it follows that
w1 ∈V (Tj).
Similarly
w1 ∈V (Ti).
Since Ti > Tj we have
wj ∈V (Ti).
Let vk ∈NG(vj). Then
V (Tj) ∩V (Tk)̸ = ∅.
If wj ∈V (Tk) then V (Ti) ∩V (Tk)̸ = ∅. Otherwise
wk ∈V (Tj)
dT(r, wk) ≤dT(r, w1)
and
w1 ∈V (Ti) ∩V (Tj)
whence
wk ∈V (Ti)
since Ti > Tj. In either event
V (Ti) ∩V (Tk)̸ = ∅
and so
vk ∈NG(vi).
Since vk was an arbitrary vertex of NG(vj), it follows that
NG(vj) ⊆NG(vi)
